Replay

Browser authority migration work

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

The native Room's migration and fencing rules remain the reference. WebRTC packet exchange and a P2P duel do not by themselves make browser authority migration safe.

Implemented and tested prerequisites:

  1. Raw WebSocket control transport, including binary/text separation, bounded queues, full-size packets and retained small reads.
  2. A real Chrome client obtains signed grants from the native SQLite-backed authority Service; a corrupted MAC is rejected. Control reconnection preserves the RPC nonce/sequence state.
  3. Native Room can use WebSocket control while retaining ENet gameplay. Planned and crash handoff use the existing checkpoint/lease/session machinery.
  4. Paired wall/monotonic clock implementation and explicit failure semantics.
  5. Pure challenged rendezvous signing/verification: room creation requires the current approved owner, rather than possession of a room code.

The native challenged signaling frontend and RTC authorization callback are now implemented. A three-browser gate rejects non-owner creation, duplicate creators, proof replay across connections and expired challenges, then exchanges full-size game packets. Room owns its browser clock, nonce provider, copied RTC configuration and grant authorization through role changes. Migration_Transport explicitly describes the RTC destination as a trusted provider URL plus a code derived from the signed view. This preserves the coordinator wire and durable-record formats.

The actual Cavecrawl browser project passes planned handoff and killed-host recovery with a surviving guest, preserved inventory/seats, and new accepted actions. Planned mode also rejoins the old host. The gate additionally covers two handoffs, control partition/fencing, successor loss during handoff and a killed host returning with a fresh incarnation. Monotonic driver receipts distinguish fault-to-action time from the narrower Room timer.

Remaining acceptance and integration:

Actual Coturn relay gates now pass Cavecrawl over UDP/TCP and Scrapyard's asset-aware combat flow over UDP. Selected browser candidate pairs and Coturn logs prove relayed traffic at join, handoff and rejoin. Incorrect relay credentials do not fall back to direct gameplay in relay-only mode. See relay evidence.

The online Cavecrawl menu now creates, joins and durably rejoins parties through the standalone room service. A real Chrome gate covers automatic successor selection, a zero-loss handoff and concurrent isolated rooms. This uses explicit loopback WS with RTC gameplay; public WSS/TURN deployment is still separate work.

  • Public account/room provisioning and trust boundaries. Authenticated signaling-only reconnect now preserves healthy channels and peer IDs; broader network/provider-outage envelopes still need measurement.
  • External asset dependencies and gameplay recovery in richer browser game ports; broader workloads and repeated timing measurements for the existing failure matrix.
  • Actual browser sleep/clock anomalies, TLS/TURN and additional browser engines.
  • Broader interruption measurements, including time before local fencing, and checkpoint age/lost ticks/transfer size under representative gameplay.

These remain required work; local planned/crash success does not establish the remaining failure matrix or public deployment envelope.

See WebSocket, paired clock and rendezvous for current APIs and limits. This completes no additional milestone by declaration; all remaining gates are part of the active M0–M9 objective.
